---
title: Pull from a vendor
description: Write a vendor's records into Marfa as items, connect the items they relate, set aside what the vendor deleted, and say which types the connector holds read only.
---

A pull reads the vendor and writes what it finds as items. [The connector kit](/build/connector) does everything below for you. This guide shows the operations underneath, in the order a run uses them, for a connector built directly on the API.

The examples follow a recipe box connector with a key of its own under the source `recipes`, which writes the type `recipes.recipe`. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a [TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk) client made with that key.

## Write what you read

[Upsert items in bulk](/api-reference/items/bulkUpsertItems) writes up to 5,000 records in one request:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items/bulk
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": "recipes.recipe",
      "source_id": "kim:r-208",
      "tier": "feed",
      "properties": { "recipe_id": "r-208", "title": "Lemon dal", "body": "Rinse the lentils…" },
      "occurred_at": "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "atomic": false
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items/bulk", {
  body: {
    items: [
      {
        type: "recipes.recipe",
        source_id: "kim:r-208",
        tier: "feed",
        properties: { recipe_id: "r-208", title: "Lemon dal", body: "Rinse the lentils…" },
        occurred_at: "2026-10-01T08:00:00Z",
      },
    ],
    atomic: false,
  },
});
```

Marfa answers each record on its own:

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "counts": { "created": 1, "updated": 0, "skipped": 0, "errored": 0 },
  "results": [{ "index": 0, "outcome": "created", "id": "01a12313-fd4a-78a1-af1e-32792c3df63b" }]
}
```

- **The natural key** is the item's `source`, taken from the key, and its `source_id`, the vendor's ID for the record. Marfa updates the item that holds it or creates one, so reading a record twice never makes a second item.
- **Put the vendor account inside the `source_id`**, as in `kim:r-208`, when the record belongs to that account. Two accounts under one source then can't share an item. The source itself names the system, never an account or the route a record came by.
- **`tier: "feed"`** puts the item in the feed, where a person or an app decides whether to keep it. **`occurred_at`** is when the record happened at the vendor.
- **`atomic: false`** writes the records that pass and reports a refused one as `errored`. By default, one refused record rolls the whole page back.
- **Write an item's text as Markdown.** Marfa stores the field a type's `body_field` names as it arrives, so convert a vendor's HTML first.

## What a repeat write does

A run usually sends records Marfa already holds. Marfa sorts them out, so you can send the vendor's page as it is:

- **A record that changes nothing** comes back `skipped`, with `reason: "unchanged"`. Marfa writes nothing, keeps the `version` and announces no event.
- **A record whose item is in the bin** comes back `skipped`, with `reason: "trashed"`. A person moved it there, and a pull never brings it back.
- **A purged record** leaves a tombstone. [Look up the items](/api-reference/items/lookupItems) under the records' keys, and the answer lists tombstones beside the items. Write a purged record again only if the vendor changed it after the tombstone's `settled_at`.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items/lookup
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "type": "recipes.recipe", "source": "recipes", "source_ids": ["kim:r-208", "kim:r-209"] }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data } = await marfa.POST("/items/lookup", {
  body: { type: "recipes.recipe", source: "recipes", source_ids: ["kim:r-208", "kim:r-209"] },
});
```

## Keep a quiet run light

A run that finds nothing new should send Marfa **a few requests, however much the connector holds**. Ask about many records at once: one lookup names many `source_ids`, and one bulk page writes thousands. Never send a request for each item you hold.

In the kit, call `held` once for each type in a run, and use `linkedEach` rather than `linked` in a loop. Every connector in marfa-connectors keeps the kit's quiet-run test, which fails when a run with nothing new sends more than one more request for each 200 items Marfa holds.

## Connect items

A record that points at another, such as a recipe in a cookbook, becomes an [edge](/build/edges) between the two items. An entry's `edges` maps an edge type to the IDs of the items it now points to:

```json title="Request body"
{
  "items": [
    {
      "type": "recipes.recipe",
      "source_id": "kim:r-208",
      "properties": { "recipe_id": "r-208", "title": "Lemon dal" },
      "edges": { "in-collection": ["01a12313-fd4e-7800-ab67-c886f1b9ef58"] }
    }
  ]
}
```

- **The list replaces that type's edges** from the item, and an edge type left out stays as it is.
- **Marfa's own edge types** need only `--edge-permission <type>=write` on the key: `attached-to`, `in-collection`, `in-thread`, `references`, `excerpt-of`, `about`, `comments-on` and `parent-of`. The [edges Catalog](/catalog/edges) lists each one's direction and what a trash does to it.
- **An edge type of your own** is registered with its ends in `from_type_constraints` and `to_type_constraints`, which needs `--metadata-permission edge_types=write` on the key.

In the kit, an entry's `connections` names targets by their link or `source_id`, and a target Marfa doesn't hold yet is connected once it arrives. To stop writing a connection, keep it in `connections` and add it to `retired`: the kit then removes only the edges it wrote, so an edge a person drew stays, and the key keeps write on that edge type.

## Set aside what the vendor deleted

When the vendor no longer has a record, [change the item's state](/api-reference/items/transitionItem) to `archived`. Don't move it to the bin, which is for people. An archived item keeps its history. A bulk write leaves an item's state alone, so if the vendor lists the record again, change the state back to `active` the same way.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items/01a12313-fd4e-7800-ab67-c886f1b9ef58/transition
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "state": "archived" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/items/{id}/transition", {
  params: { path: { id: "01a12313-fd4e-7800-ab67-c886f1b9ef58" } },
  body: { state: "archived" },
});
```

Be **sure the vendor deleted it**. A partial listing, such as one page or open records only, says nothing about a record it leaves out, so ask about that record first.

## Name the source

Apps show a source by its name and mark, an icon. [Read the source](/api-reference/sources/getSource) on each start, and [set](/api-reference/sources/updateSource) only what it lacks, so a name the owner chose stays:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
PATCH /sources/recipes
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "name": "Recipe box", "mark": "lucide:chef-hat" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.PATCH("/sources/{source}", {
  params: { path: { source: "recipes" } },
  body: { name: "Recipe box", mark: "lucide:chef-hat" },
});
```

A key may set its own source and the sources it claims. The kit does this from `sourceName` and `sourceMark`. If Marfa refuses, the kit logs a warning, runs anyway and tries again on the next start.

## Declare the types you don't carry back

A connector that takes no edits back for a type puts back, on its next run, any edit a person makes to its items in Marfa. Name those types in `read_only_types` when you [register the connector](/api-reference/connectors/registerConnector), and their items read `read_only: true`, so an app can show them locked:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "name": "recipes", "read_only_types": ["recipes.cookbook"] }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/connectors", {
  body: { name: "recipes", read_only_types: ["recipes.cookbook"] },
});
```

- **Each registration replaces the list**, and one without it clears the list. Build it on every start from what the connector carries back with its current settings. The kit lists every type it writes and doesn't carry back.
- **An item reads `true` only while every live connector** of its source lists its type and may write it.
- **Marfa refuses no edit** to a read-only item. The flag says what the connector will do.

The rules behind this page are in the [connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md) and [items](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/items.md#bulk-writes) chapters of the contract.
